title: One Election to a Trip: Holding Keyturn Guest Protection Plan Elections
content:
Protection under the Keyturn Guest Protection Plan is elected trip by trip, so a guest holds one election
for each trip and may hold as many elections as they have trips, with no ceiling on the number. One trip carries
exactly one live election, and a second quote raised on a trip that already carries one is a duplicate to be
voided rather than a second cover. Each election stands on its own terms, so the level chosen on one trip never
carries over to the next and the guest chooses again each time.

## The rule as three conditions

| The situation | What follows |
|---|---|
| A guest has several trips running or booked at once | They may hold one election against each of those trips, and the marketplace sets no ceiling on how many |
| A trip already carries a live election and a second quote is raised on the same trip | The second quote is a duplicate, and a duplicate is voided rather than treated as a second cover |
| A guest held one level on an earlier trip and a new trip is quoted | The earlier choice does not carry over, and the guest chooses again for the new trip |

## A hypothetical portfolio

A guest with a weekend car booked for next month, a car currently out on a trip and a month-long reservation
beginning in the spring holds three trips and may hold three elections, one against each. Nothing in the plan
caps that number. If a second quote were raised against the month-long reservation while the first quote on it
still stood, the marketplace would have two quotes on one trip: the second is the duplicate, and a duplicate is
voided rather than allowed to run as a second cover alongside the first. The level the guest took on the car
currently out on a trip has no bearing at all on which level they may take for the spring reservation.
